title: The Zscaler MCP server: release, protocol and where its behavior is described

prose.text: This walks the subjects that describe the Zscaler MCP server as a tool: which tools it registers, how writes and deletes are gated, what a tool result contains, and how an HTTP deployment is secured. Product-specific MCP tool behavior is described in the product subjects that use it. {{release}}

prose.label: Where to read next.
prose.text: Which tools exist on a given server is in [[shared.mcp-server.tool-inventory]]; how creates, updates and deletes are gated is in [[shared.mcp-server.delete-confirmation]]; what a result carries (full records, untrusted-content banners, JMESPath, CSV) is in [[shared.mcp-server.results]]; TLS, Host validation, client authentication, logging and cloud secrets are in [[shared.mcp-server.http-deployment]]; where the server's argument converters drop or choose silently (ZPA policy conditions, ZTW country names) is in [[shared.mcp-server.argument-conversion]].

prose.label: Product examples.
prose.text: ZPA list paging through MCP is in [[zpa.api.pagination]], and the Sandbox report banner in [[zia.sandbox.report]].

checks.do: Which MCP server release the deployment runs, since the write gate and the confirmation channels changed in 0.15.0.
Which Python SDK version the MCP installation actually resolved, before tracing a tool's behavior to SDK code.

release.statement: The pinned MCP server tree declares package version 0.15.4 and requires Python >=3.11,<4.0.

sdk-does-api-calls.statement: The MCP server calls Zscaler through the Python SDK, which does every API call, token exchange, pagination and retry; the server's package metadata leaves `zscaler-sdk-python` unconstrained so installs pull the latest SDK.

quotes: Transport / auth shim — UNCHANGED from v1. The SDK still does every

Intentionally unconstrained so installs always pull the latest SDK

dependency-floor.statement: The server requires `mcp[cli]>=2.0.0,<3`; 2.0.0 is the floor because the `2026-07-28` revision features (`InputRequiredResult`, `RequestStateSecurity`, `cache_hints`) land there. Standalone `fastmcp` is not a dependency of any auth mode, and a test fails if it becomes a base dependency.

quotes: The floor is 2.0.0 because that is where the `2026-07-28` revision lands:
Standalone `fastmcp` is not a dependency of any auth mode

lock-resolution.statement: The MCP tree's generated requirements resolve `mcp==2.0.0` and `zscaler-sdk-python==1.9.43`, while the Python SDK vendored in this repository is version 1.11.3; the lock file's own editable entry for `zscaler-mcp` still says 0.15.3.

protocol-negotiated.statement: Version 0.15.0 adopted the `2026-07-28` MCP revision; clients on older revisions keep working because the revision is negotiated per connection, with nothing to configure.

quotes: **Adopted the `2026-07-28` MCP revision.** Clients on older revisions continue to work unchanged — the revision is negotiated per connection, with nothing to configure on either side.

conformance-gate.statement: CI gates on the conformance scenarios of the published 2025-11-25 revision; a separate baseline for the 2026-07-28 revision runs on a prerelease runner and does not gate CI.

quotes: every scenario in the "active" suite for the published 2025-11-25 protocol
